sentences.text: Shri Satyapal Chadhar - Government Adv  respondent/State.
Heard on admission.
This appeal is admitted for hearing.
Record of the trial court has been received.
Also heard on I.A. No.29221/2023, an application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to appellant.

The appellant has been convicted under Section 420/120-B of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 7 years and fine of Rs.15,00,000/-, Section 409/120-B of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and fine of Rs. 20,00,000/- with default stipulations.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that learned trial Court has acquitted appellant of the offence pertaining to M.P. Nikshepakon Ke hiton Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam but learned trial Court has convicted and sentenced appellant for offence under Section 420/120-B and 409/120-B of IPC.

entities.text: M.P. Nikshepakon Ke hiton Ka Sanrakshan Adhiniyam

sentences.text: Further, after referring to testimonies of Gagan Sanodiya (PW-1) and Santkumar Chandravanshi (PW-2), it is urged that initially, amount deposited by the witness was returned to him and thereafter, witness also deposited an amount of Rs. 3,00,000/- and maturity period of aforesaid 2 CRA-15454-2023 deposit was year 2024 and present complaint has been filed prior to that in the year 2020.
Further, after referring to testimony of Santkumar Chandravanshi (PW-2), it is urged that the witness has not produced any document pertaining to any deposit by him.

Further,
prosecution witnesses Gagan Sanodiya (PW-1) and Satish Jaiswal (PW-3) have admitted in their cross-examination that appellant did not cheat them in any manner whatsoever.

Satish Jaiswal (PW-3) also stated in para 13 of his deposition that he did not deposit any amount with Ashok Ashok Choudhary vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126163525/
1 Choudhary.

sentences.text: It is also urged that appellant is in jail since 28.12.2020.
He further submits that, there is no possibility of early hearing of this appeal in near future Thus, remaining jail sentence of appellant may be suspended.
Learned counsel for the respondent/State, on the other hand, has opposed the application.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused record of the case.

Having regard to testimonies of Gagan Sanodiya (PW-1), Santkumar Chandravanshi (PW-2) and Satish Jaiswal (PW-3) and custody period of appellant, I deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of appellant.
Accordingly, aforesaid I.A is allowed.

Subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended and it is directed that he be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.15,000/- (Rupees Fifteen Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court with a further direction 3 CRA-15454-2023 to appear before the concerning trial Court on 08.09.2025 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by the trial court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE L.R.
